reviewContext.userProblem: An iPhone app design drawn with nodetto-cli 0.8.9 came out misaligned and sloppy. Defects D1-D10: ui.control ignores textAlign (D1); tabs ignore fill/stroke/accent and options are not styleable (D2); newline labels render monospace on one line (D3); geo rects under 3 units vanish (D4); no precise text layer, text.note ignores fontSize/fontWeight on update (D5); no icon element (D6); elements added inside a frame are not its children and nothing clips or snaps (D7); auto layout cannot be driven from the CLI (D8); prototype links are drawn across artboards with verbose labels and there is no prototype view, flow start, storyboard or presentation (D9); frame titles overlap content and there is no easy per-frame side-by-side comparison (D10).
requiredOutcomes: Decision 1: precise text layer on text.note (text:layer shape, no implicit padding, auto-width/auto-height/fixed, alignment, font size/weight, line height, letter spacing, color, single-line ellipsis, honored on add and update).

Decision 2: ui.icon element backed by vendored Lucide (ISC) with LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, name lookup from palette and `nodetto-cli shapes icon <query>`, size/color/stroke width, custom SVG path icons.
Decision 3: dividers and borders of any thickness >= 0.5 render; per-side borders and stroke alignment.

Decision 4: ui.control honors alignment, padding, font, color, radius, leading/trailing icons; tabs/segmented with underline and pill indicators, selected/unselected colors, per-option overrides; badges.
Decision 5: iOS component kit on the component/instance system with overridable properties, insertable by ios:<name> shape ID from palette and CLI.

Decision 6: frame auto-parenting (CLI add with parent or by containment), children move with frame, clip content, safe-area and layout-grid guides, iPhone presets including 390x844 and 402x874, titles above the artboard.
Decision 7: CLI layout/sizing (direction, gap, padding, alignment, hug/fill/fixed, absolute children), align, distribute, snap, and an 8/4 point desktop snap grid.

Decision 8: Figma-style prototyping concepts: hotspot or frame links with trigger/action (incl. back, swap-overlay)/animation, prototype view toggle with curved compact links, named flow starts, storyboard overview, desktop and HTML click-through presentation with persistent elements.
Decision 9: app-design lint (off-frame, text overflow/truncation, overlapping controls, off-grid, misaligned siblings, touch targets under 44 points).
Decision 10: export of all frames of a page as individual PNGs and a side-by-side comparison helper in CLI (`compare`) and desktop app.

Item 11: reproduction of the ten private reference screens built only through nodetto-cli operations into the operator-named git-ignored output directory, validate and app lint with zero findings, prototype links and one flow start, per-frame PNGs compared side by side with every reference screenshot (drift <= 4 points, correct icons, colors and type).
Generic iPhone sample under examples/ exercising the kit and prototype flows; CLI help and docs for AI agents.
TypeScript and native Rust CLI parity covered by mise run test-cli; final gates mise run verify, test-cli, build-cli and typecheck with no new failures versus the ipd-00 baseline.
nonGoals: No server, auth or deployment code (public repo).
No proprietary Figma assets or internal names; concepts only.
No schemaVersion bump or migration; all additions are optional fields plus the ui.icon type and two prototype action values.
No new native Rust host primitive is planned; parity comes from running shared TypeScript in the Boa-hosted CLI.
No push, merge, rebase, release, signing or upload; no changes to other repos or worktrees.
No tracked copy of any private reference material (names, texts, colors, screenshots).
constraints: Work only in /Users/taco/gits/tacogips/nodetto-app-iphone-design on feat/iphone-app-design from f59bef4; gitPush false.
Privacy: reference and reproduction directories stay under git-ignored tmp/; ipd-28 scans tracked and untracked files against tmp/ipd-s772/ipd-27-reproduction/private-terms.txt.
AGENTS.md: CARGO_TERM_QUIET=true, no emojis, stage by explicit path, no tool attribution in commits.
Existing documents stay valid and render byte-identically except the rows in the design's Accepted output changes table.
Problems outside a unit's writePaths are findings, never blockers; finding statuses use the fixed vocabulary.

Step 5 IPD-R8 repair: the normalization does not depend on id order. Stdout and stderr mask every generated id and printed prefix to the single token <ID>. created arrays keep operation order (apps/cli/src/edit/batch.ts:301); any stdout list the CLI sorts by id is compared as a sorted masked list and recorded. Documents: parse each JSONL record, compute its masked canonical text (generated ids deep-replaced by <ID>, object keys sorted), and assign ordinals ID1..IDn by sorting on (masked page, memberIds containment depth, masked canonical text). The ordinals are used only to print the failure diff. Records that tie on all three keys are interchangeable (multiset semantics). Equality requires (a) equal sorted lists of masked canonical record texts and (b) equal sorted lists of reference edges maskedText(source)|fieldPath-with-array-index|maskedText(target). Pitfall: packages/io/src/jsonl/serialize.ts:146-152 sorts elements by page and then by element id. ULIDs minted in the same millisecond (packages/core/src/ids.ts:38-40, packages/core/src/editor/components.ts:162 and 289) therefore order randomly, so file order is not stable across hosts. Required plain-test self-checks: permuted generated ids with a different id-sorted line order -> equal; a changed non-id field (visual.x or a prop) on a minted element -> not equal; child memberships swapped between two distinct frames -> not equal. The test file is run three times, and each run must exit 0 with 0 fail and 0 skip. harness.ts, serialize.ts, ids.ts and engine source stay unchanged. PNG outputs keep the round-12 decoded RGBA comparison. Then complete the remaining DR-02 and clean-kit lint cases. Keep the ipd-24 work already in the working tree and continue from it.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: The exact compareFile contract cannot hold for operations that mint ids independently in each runtime; ipd-23 passed by avoiding id-minting edits. A normalizer that only rewrites generated ids keeps every other byte under test, so real behavioral drift still fails.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: 2026-11-10 operator amendment round 14 (session-796 wave 1): Z-order comparison (operator round 14, binding): an element's fractional z-order `index` is randomized when the element is created, independently in Bun and native, so the normalized comparison must NOT compare raw `index` strings of elements created by the compared edit. Instead, per page, sort all elements by `index` (the engine's ordering) and assert the two hosts yield the same sequence of normalized element ids (ID placeholders and fixed ids). Raw `index` values of elements that already existed in the input document are compared exactly. Every other field is compared exactly after id normalization. Do not change engine or harness code.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Round 13's relative-order clause was lost when step 4 rewrote the plan, so ipd-24 compared randomized fractional indexes exactly and failed (2 of 4). Relative z-order of the normalized ids preserves the behavior under test (stacking order) without depending on random index strings. The rule is now in ipd-24's manifest acceptanceCriteria so a plan rewrite cannot drop it.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: 2026-11-10 operator amendment round 15 (session-797 wave 1): Generated-value comparison (operator round 15, binding; supersedes the narrower round-13 and round-14 wording): an edit may create values at random independently in Bun and native. In the normalized comparison: (1) every generated identifier (element ids, page ids, any ULID-like id and its printed short prefix) is replaced with ordinal placeholders by first appearance; (2) every generated ordering key, meaning element `index`, page `order` and any other fractional ordering key that the compared edit created, is not compared as a string; instead assert that both hosts give the same order of the normalized ids within that collection (pages sorted by `order`; elements per page sorted by `index`); (3) every value that already existed in the input document, and every other field, is compared exactly after normalization. Do not change engine or harness code.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Kit insertion also creates an iOS kit page whose `order` key is randomized independently per host; round 14 covered only element indexes. Generalizing to every generated id and ordering key keeps the behavior under test (which elements and pages exist, their content and their order) while ignoring only random tokens.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: 2026-11-10 operator amendment round 16 (session-799 wave 2): ipd-24-parity-flows is an accepted dependency. The committed example document is generated once and committed; its own regression test validates it, lints it with zero findings and renders it, but does not regenerate it byte for byte. Do not change engine id generation.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: ipd-26 found that two identical kit-insertion edits produce documents with 16 different generated ids, so an exact-byte determinism gate can never pass; ipd-27 (reproduction) and ipd-28 (finish) would hit the same wall, so the contract is set for all three at once instead of one round per unit.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: 2026-11-10 operator amendment round 17 (session-801 wave 1): Kit quality fix (operator round 17, binding): ipd-26-example-sample owns the iOS kit sources and tests (packages/core/src/kits/ios/bars.ts, content.ts, style.ts, insert.ts, props.ts, types.ts, kit-core.test.ts, kit-content.test.ts). (c) Afterwards every default kit component, inserted with its defaults into a 390x844 iPhone frame, lints with zero findings; add one regression test that inserts each kit component and asserts zero app-design lint findings. Do not change the lint rules. Update existing kit test expectations only where (a) or (b) changes a number. (d) The sample's prototype links target the specific child control (tab item, back button, send button) inside the kit instance, not the whole instance, and no link label overlaps another control. designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: The generic sample's zero-findings lint gate failed with 19 warnings: 16 app-off-grid on children of kit instances (fractional coordinates from unrounded centering), 2 note-overflow in kit text boxes 18 high whose default text needs two lines, and 1 label collision in the sample's own links. designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: 2026-11-10 operator amendment round 18 (session-802 wave 2): ipd-26-example-sample is an accepted dependency. Layout rule (operator round 18, binding for every reproduction part): the reference screenshots are a 390x844 web view with no iOS status bar or home indicator. In each 390x844 iPhone frame: iOS status bar 0-47; top-anchored content shifted +47; bottom-anchored chrome (tab bar, floating action buttons, composer) shifted up by the 34-point home indicator, with the home indicator below it; the empty middle absorbs the difference. Where shifted top content would collide with bottom chrome (one screen in this set), that content area is a scroll region: put the content inside a frame clipped at the top edge of the tab bar (clip content on), so rows below the visible area are hidden as in the running app; floating action buttons stay as an intentional overlay above the content exactly as in the reference. Compare such a screen with two bands (top content above the clip line, bottom chrome) and record the number of clipped rows in the progress log by number only. The reproduction is split into sequential parts sharing one document: ipd-27a-reproduction-chrome (shared chrome + screens 01-03) -> ipd-27b-reproduction-detail (04-06) -> ipd-27c-reproduction-search-more (07-10) -> ipd-27-reproduction (links, flow start, full gates, all comparisons, copy). Keep the ipd-27 work already in tmp/ipd-s772/ipd-27-reproduction and continue from it.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: ipd-27 asked for an approved treatment of one screen where the +47/-35 shifts make the content overlap the bottom chrome; the running app scrolls that content under the tab bar with the floating buttons overlaid, so a clipped scroll region reproduces it faithfully. designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: 2026-11-10 operator amendment round 19 (session-805 wave 1): Kit fix (operator round 19, binding for ipd-27a): ipd-27a-reproduction-chrome owns the iOS kit sources and tests. (a) The tab bar distributes its item widths in whole points for any item count (the widths sum to the bar width; for example 98, 97, 98, 97 for four items on 390), and places every icon, label and badge on the 1-point grid, with or without a badge. (b) The default floating action button has no offset dark shadow (no visible crescent); use none or a subtle centered shadow. Add kit regression tests: a tab bar with 2 to 5 items, with and without a badge, and a floating action button each lint with zero findings. Do not change lint rules. Reproduction lint gate (operator round 19, binding for ipd-27a, ipd-27b, ipd-27c, ipd-27-reproduction and ipd-28-finish; replaces the plain zero-findings wording for the reproduction document only): `app-off-grid`, `note-overflow`, `app-text-overflow`, touch-target, overlap and every error must be zero. `app-misaligned` ("nearly aligns") findings are allowed only for elements whose position matches the reference screenshot within 4 points, because the reference itself is not pixel-aligned; record their count per screen in the progress log. designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: 2026-11-10 operator amendment round 21 (session-808 wave 1): Shared center line (operator round 21, binding for ipd-27k): within each tab-bar slot, the icon, the label box and the badge anchor share one whole-point center line. Compute the slot's integer center c = slot.x + floor(slot.width / 2) (relative to the bar), place the icon at c - icon.width/2 (icon widths are even), and give the label box an even width (slot.width, minus 1 when slot.width is odd) with x = c - labelWidth/2, so the icon and label centers coincide exactly and every value is a whole point. Rewriting label and indicator geometry for this purpose is authorized even though their integer assertions pass. Lint rules stay unchanged; the zero-findings regression for 2 to 5 items with and without a badge (and the 402-point bar) must pass.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: After whole-point rounding, odd-width slots (for example 97 on a 390 bar with four items) put a 24-wide icon center at 48 while a full-slot label box centers at 48.5; app-misaligned correctly reports the half-point offset (3 findings, kit tests 17/18). Sharing one integer center line removes the offset without touching lint.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: 2026-11-11 step 4 s810 (resolves S5-s809-1): the ipd-27k plan body is reconciled with the binding round-21 center line. The Math.round icon and badge offsets are replaced by c = slot.x + floor(slot.width / 2). Label and Indicator are rewritten to the even-width box at c - width/2 and join Icon, Badge and BadgeBackground in the single keepMembers set. The bars.ts tab build uses the same center line. Badge and badge background top move to slot y + 3. insert.ts passes count on a tab-bar width change. Measured state updated to 17 pass, 1 fail, 3 app-misaligned. The round-20 and round-21 verbatim sections are unchanged.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: A read-only Step 4 simulation through the public editor API (tmp/ipd-s772/plan-check/step4-s810/sim.log and sim-badge-y.log) shows three things. The center line alone clears every no-badge case. A visible badge still gets 2 app-misaligned findings until its top equals the icon top. designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: 2026-11-10 operator amendment round 22 (session-809 wave 2): ipd-27k-kit-grid is an accepted dependency. Scratch rule (operator round 22, binding for every remaining plan): temporary directories that test harnesses create under the operating system temp dir (mkdtemp under os.tmpdir(), for example nodetto-*-parity-*) are authorized scratch and are not write-scope violations. The reproduction plans do not run the native parity suites (they belong to accepted ipd-23 and ipd-24); their required gates are build-cli plus the reproduction gates. Rebuild rule (operator round 22, binding for ipd-27a, ipd-27b, ipd-27c and ipd-27-reproduction): the reproduction document is rebuilt from an empty document on the fixed kit by a generator script kept under tmp/ipd-s772/ipd-27-reproduction/ (git-ignored). The script writes the ops files and applies them with nodetto-cli edit. Ops never hard-code generated element ids: build each screen in one edit batch using `ref` and `@ref`, and resolve cross-batch targets (for example prototype link targets) by element name through nodetto-cli inspect --format json inside the script. Each part reruns the script from scratch for its screens plus all earlier parts, so the document always reflects the current kit.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: ipd-27a blocked because the native parity test it ran writes mkdtemp scratch under the OS temp dir, which the gate read as outside its artifact roots; the preserved reproduction was built before the kit fix (66 lint findings, 20 hard) and its correction ops hard-code generated ids from that document, so it must be rebuilt by a script that never depends on generated ids.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: 2026-11-11 step 4 s811 (round-22 consistency; the imported Step 5 findings IPD-R1, IPD-R2 and IPD-R3 were already resolved by round 1 and are re-confirmed): the ipd-27a header dependsOn no longer names the accepted ipd-27k-kit-grid. The s808 rule that kept the ipd-27a native parity item 10 is superseded and the item is removed, and the manifest acceptance text no longer mentions native-parity tests. All four reproduction plans get one shared generator contract: gen/build.ts --through <NN>, a rebuild from an empty document, ref/@ref inside each batch, name lookup through inspect --format json across batches, no literal generated ids, and the pre-fix ops/ files kept as reference only. Plan IDs, dependsOn, writePaths, sharedPaths, artifactRoots and verification strings are unchanged.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Operator round 22 made ipd-27k accepted, removed native parity from the reproduction gates and required a script rebuild. Before this change, ipd-27a still kept the parity gate and still named ipd-27k as pending, and the plans did not say how the serial parts share one generator.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: 2026-11-11 step 4 s812 (review finding S5-s811-1): in the generator contract of ipd-27a, ipd-27b, ipd-27c and ipd-27-reproduction, cross-batch references are written into gen/ops/ as names (name:<exact name>, or select+where{name,page}+expect 1 then @ref), and the flow start is an update with id name:<start frame name>. inspect --format json is only a check that each name is unique before a batch is written. The s811 grep count is replaced by a fail-closed literal-id gate, added to each of the four verification lists after validate. It rejects a full 26-character Crockford id under any key or in any array, an id prefix as the whole value of id, target, parent, page, from or to or inside memberIds or ids, and indented ops lines, and it exits 2 when gen/ops/ is empty. Step 4 tested it on 10 scratch samples (tmp/ipd-s772/plan-check/step4-s812/gates.log). For ipd-27a, ipd-27b and ipd-27c, a new acceptance criterion states that the round-18 Scope wording ('ops files under .../ops/', 'appending to the document the previous part left') is superseded by the round-22 rebuild rule. designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: The s811 text told the script to put ids found through inspect into gen/ops/ while its own regex counted such ids as failures, and that regex missed connect from/to, page and arrays. The CLI already resolves name: and select+where within a batch, and rejects missing or ambiguous names, so no id ever needs to be written. The round-18 Scope wording still described appending to an existing document, which contradicted the round-22 rebuild.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: 2026-11-10 operator amendment round 23 (session-811 wave 1): ipd-27a-reproduction-chrome is accepted by the operator after visual inspection of its three comparisons (all elements within 4 points, icons/colors/weight correct, one badge about 2 points off). For each screen, export the frame and run nodetto-cli compare against its reference with the 4-point grid. If the comparison shows the flagged elements within 4 points of their reference positions, record a single line per screen in the progress log: screen number, count of app-misaligned findings, and 'within 4 points of reference'. A part is done when hard findings are zero, the per-screen lines are recorded, and the operator-style visual checklist (positions within 4 points, icons, colors, weight, nothing missing) is met for its screens. Do not spend continuations on cosmetic differences under 4 points.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: ipd-27a rebuilt the document on the fixed kit and passed every gate except its own per-finding justification of 32 app-misaligned near-alignments, which exhausted its continuations. designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: 2026-11-11 operator amendment round 24 (session-812 wave 1): new root unit ipd-27p-native-edit-perf; ipd-27b-reproduction-detail depends on it. Native edit performance (operator round 24, binding): native nodetto-cli edit scales superlinearly with document size (a synthetic-like 135-operation batch takes over 90 s on a 300-element document, batches on 151/233/298 elements take 6/39/59 s), while the Bun CLI runs the same batches in about 1 s. macOS sample shows the time in the embedded Boa engine's garbage collector (GcHeader inc_ref_count, GC dropping, mark_heap), which points to per-operation work proportional to the whole document (cloning, rescanning or reserializing the document or its indexes for every operation, for example in auto-parenting containment, selection or kit insertion). Profile with `bun --cpu-prof` and with `sample` on the native binary, find the per-operation O(document) work in the edit path, and make batch application near-linear without changing any result (all parity, edit and kit tests stay green). Add a generic synthetic regression to apps/cli/src/native-parity/edit-performance.test.ts: build about 300 elements in several 390x844 iPhone frames over 3 to 4 edit batches that use parent, select and kit insertion; assert every native batch finishes in under 3 s and the batch on the largest document takes under 3 times the first batch. No private reference content in the fixture.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: ipd-27b's screen 05 native edit stayed CPU-bound for over six minutes. The operator reproduced it: native batch times grow superlinearly (1/6/39/59 s at 97/151/233/298 elements, over 90 s for the next batch) while Bun takes about 1 s; the profile is dominated by Boa GC activity, so the edit path does per-operation whole-document work. A 300-element app design is small, so this is a product defect to fix before the reproduction continues.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: 2026-11-11 operator amendment round 25 (session-814 wave 1): Performance target and scratch (operator round 25, binding for ipd-27p and every remaining plan): the git-ignored apps/desktop/tmp/ directory created by existing test suites is authorized scratch, like OS temp directories. designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: The operator re-timed the reproduction batches on the new build: 1.3/2.5/3.0/7.7 s at 151/233/298/457 elements (previously 6/39/59/over 90 s), so the defect that blocked the reproduction is fixed in practice. ipd-27p stopped only because a required suite writes git-ignored scratch under apps/desktop/tmp/ and its largest synthetic batches sit slightly above 3 s.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: 2026-11-11 operator amendment round 26 (session-815 wave 1): General scratch rule (operator round 26, binding for every remaining plan; supersedes the narrower round-22 and round-25 scratch wording): files that test harnesses or CLI commands write while running a plan's required verification are not write-scope violations when they land in git-ignored scratch: anywhere under the repository tmp/ (including other plans' tmp/ipd-s772/* artifact roots, for example tmp/ipd-s772/ipd-26-example-sample/ written by apps/cli/src/native-parity/iphone-kit-example.test.ts), apps/desktop/tmp/, target/, or the operating system temp directory. A plan's own source edits must still stay within its writePaths, and `git status --porcelain` must show no new tracked or untracked non-ignored files outside them.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: ipd-27p met the round-25 performance target (synthetic regression 5/5 passed, batches 2.2-3.8 s, down from 8.1-21.3 s) but blocked a third time on scratch: the accepted ipd-26 example test writes into tmp/ipd-s772/ipd-26-example-sample/.
